summary: Norlane: sudden conversation-lag spike across dedicated pool and restore playbook
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-10 02:12 UTC Norlane reported a sudden spike in conversational response latency for their dedicated GPU pool. Multiple user sessions experienced delays of 5–30s per token and several streaming responses stalled for >10s before resuming. Customer-facing latency and timeouts began at ~02:05 UTC and peaked by 02:25 UTC.

Impact:
- Affects Norlane production tenant on dedicated pool (no other customers reported issues from initial triage).
- Increased p50/p95 token latency; several 5xx errors from serving-runtime for long-running streams.
- Customer saw degraded UX and began routing traffic to fallback endpoints; potential billing exposure for replayed requests.

Timeline (abridged):
- 02:05 UTC: First Norlane alert via support channel.
- 02:12 UTC: Ticket created; initial triage by Support (Maya).
- 02:18 UTC: SRE alerted; Autoscaler and serving runtime teams paged.
- 02:30 UTC: Temporary routing to warm standby in another pool applied for a subset of traffic.
- 03:05 UTC: Partial restoration observed after prefix-cache priming and manual instance drain.
- 04:00 UTC: Customer requested post-incident plan; escalation opened to account team.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Send multi-turn chat requests with long context windows (>1,500 tokens) to Norlane's pinned model (gptx-13b-v2).
2. High QPS mixed with many unique session prefixes; observe KV-cache miss ratio climb and tail latency increase.
3. Streaming connections occasionally block for extended token generation.

Logs & telemetry pointers:
- Serving runtime traces: trace-id prefix 'INC-2026-0310-07-*' in datadog.
- Autoscaler events: cluster-drain and scale-down noted ~01:58-02:04 UTC (see log stream).
- KV cache hit-rate dashboard: http://dashboards.internal/kv-cache/norlane (hit-rate dropped from 92% to 22% across pool).
- Kernel selection warnings for quantized variant: kernel-compat-warn in runtime logs for instances serving gptx-13b-quant-4bit.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Temporarily pinned Norlane routing to a warm steady pool to avoid noisy scale events.
- Increased per-tenant prefix-cache retention for affected pool to reduce cold misses.
- Suspended non-critical background rebalances in autoscaler for 30m window.
- Applied streaming buffer back-pressure tune to reduce head-of-line blocking.

Customer communication summary:
- 02:40 UTC: Notified Norlane support lead (Elena Ortiz) that we detected cache eviction storm and are working on mitigations.
- 03:15 UTC: Confirmed partial restoration and continued monitoring; offered incident postmortem.

Requested next actions (playbook):
- Short term (24h): replicate reproduction in staging using Norlane traffic pattern ETL; keep dedicated pool pinned to increased cache retention; throttle high-fanout adopters in tenant.
- Medium term (7d): implement prefix grouping heuristic to reduce unique prefix cardinality effect; add autoscaler cooldown policy per-tenant.
- Long term (30d+): improve quantized-variant kernel compatibility checks and add early-detection alert for KV-hit-rate drop below 50% per-pool.
comments: 2026-03-10 02:14 UTC - Maya Chen (Support): Initial triage - high tail latency for Norlane dedicated pool, paging SRE.

2026-03-10 02:20 UTC - SRE on-call (Jonas Weber): Observed parallel scale-down events and aggressive cache eviction around 01:58-02:04 UTC; hypothesis: autoscaler rebalance coincident with high new-prefix QPS.

2026-03-10 03:10 UTC - Elena Ortiz (Norlane): Customer confirms partial improvement but reports intermittent 10s token stalls still visible; requests root-cause and timeline.

investigation_notes: KV-cache: Sudden drop in hit-rate corresponds with burst of unique session prefixes (long context, many users spinning up new sessions).
Autoscaler: Observed a sequence of scale-down/scale-up actions that likely triggered cold instance allocations while prefix cardinality was high.
Kernel selection: A subset of requests routed to gptx-13b-quant-4bit reported kernel-compatibility warnings causing increased CPU fallback paths and token generation stalls.
Hypothesis: Combined effect of prefix-cardinality storm + autoscaler rebalance + quantized-kernel mismatch produced high tail latency and streaming stalls.
Confirmed reproduction in isolated staging using Norlane-sampled traffic with artificial autoscaler churn reproduces latency spike within 2-3 minutes.
resolution_notes: Immediate fix: Pinned Norlane traffic to warm steady pool; increased cache retention and disabled aggressive rebalances for the pool (completed 02:30 UTC).
Medium fix: Deploy autoscaler cooldown patch (github.com/redwood/inference@pr/4839) to prevent per-tenant scale thrashing; rollout canary started 2026-03-12.
Kernel fix: Add preflight kernel compatibility check for quantized variants and a safety-fallback to 16-bit variant when warning threshold breached (PR opened github.com/redwood/runtime@pr/4921).
Customer remediation: Agreed on 20% credit for the incident window and scheduled a postmortem review with Norlane on 2026-03-15.
Follow-ups assigned: Implement prefix grouping heuristic (owner: Runtime team, due 2026-03-24); add KV-hit-rate alert (owner: Observability, due 2026-03-17).
